fields.label: Surgery grade
opts: Minor (e.g. excision of skin lesion, drainage of breast abscess)
Intermediate (e.g. inguinal hernia repair, tonsillectomy, knee arthroscopy)
Major or complex (e.g. hysterectomy, thyroidectomy, joint replacement, colonic resection)

fields.label: Setting
opts: Inpatient with planned HDU or ICU bed

fields.label: ASA physical status
opts: ASA I: a normal healthy patient
ASA II: a patient with mild systemic disease
ASA III: a patient with severe systemic disease
ASA IV: a patient with severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life
ASA V: a moribund patient who is not expected to survive without the operation
ASA VI: a declared brain-dead patient whose organs are being removed for donor purposes

fields.label: Emergency operation (add E to the ASA class)
Comorbidities and how well controlled
fields.hint: e.g. type 2 diabetes on insulin, HbA1c 8.2%; hypertension, BP 150/90 today

fields.label: Previous anaesthetic details
fields.hint: year, operation, type of anaesthetic, any problem

fields.label: Smoking, tobacco and alcohol
fields.hint: e.g. smokes 10 a day, advised to stop

fields.label: Mallampati class
opts: Class I: soft palate, fauces, uvula and pillars seen
Class II: soft palate, fauces and uvula seen
Class III: soft palate and base of uvula seen
Class IV: soft palate not seen

fields.label: Neck movement
opts: Fixed neck (e.g. ankylosing spondylitis, previous fusion)

fields.label: Jaw protrusion (upper lip bite test)
opts: Class 1: lower incisors bite above the vermilion border
Class 2: lower incisors bite below the vermilion border
Class 3: cannot bite the upper lip

fields.label: Teeth details
fields.hint: e.g. loose upper left central incisor, upper denture

fields.label: Other airway features
fields.hint: e.g. beard, short thick neck, goitre, facial or neck surgery or radiotherapy

fields.label: Previous difficult airway
opts: Yes, documented in records or alert letter

fields.label: High-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic or suprainguinal vascular)
Functional capacity
opts: 4 METs or more: climbs two flights of stairs without stopping
Under 4 METs: cannot climb two flights of stairs
Cannot be assessed (limited by joints, pain or disability)

fields.label: Heart and lung examination
fields.hint: e.g. S1 S2 normal, no murmur; chest clear

fields.label: ECG findings
fields.hint: e.g. sinus rhythm 78/min, no ischaemic changes

fields.label: Tired or sleepy in the daytime
Observed to stop breathing or choke in sleep
Known sleep apnoea
opts: Yes, uses CPAP at night (bring machine)

fields.label: Medicines to continue, including the morning of surgery
Medicines to stop or change, and when
fields.hint: as agreed with the prescribing team, per protocol

fields.label: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet plan
fields.hint: follow the perioperative anticoagulation protocol; record who advised

fields.label: Diabetes medicines plan
fields.hint: e.g. insulin and SGLT2 inhibitor plan as per protocol, first on the list

sections.title: Red flags before anaesthesia
sections.alert: Red flag present: discuss with the consultant anaesthetist and the surgeon before listing. Defer elective surgery until the problem is assessed and optimised; for urgent surgery, plan senior-led anaesthesia.

fields.label: Anticipated difficult airway or previous failed intubation
Active chest infection, or asthma or COPD not controlled
Recent myocardial infarction, unstable angina or new chest pain
Murmur with symptoms (breathlessness, chest pain, syncope), e.g. aortic stenosis
Personal or family history of malignant hyperthermia
Pain relief plan after surgery
fields.hint: e.g. multimodal analgesia, wound infiltration, nerve block

fields.label: Special requirements
fields.hint: e.g. difficult airway trolley, blood cross-matched, HDU or ICU bed, CPAP after surgery

fields.label: Anaesthetic options, benefits and risks discussed
Written informed consent for anaesthesia taken

orderSets.label: Pre-op: fit adult, minor or intermediate surgery (only if indicated)
Pre-op: major surgery or ASA III and above
Pre-op: heart disease, cardiac risk factors or age 65 and over

advice.title: Getting ready for your anaesthetic
advice.text: If you smoke, stopping for several weeks before the operation makes your anaesthetic safer, and do not smoke on the day of the operation. If you are very overweight, losing weight lowers the risks. Get loose teeth or crowns seen by a dentist before the operation. Bring a list of all your medicines, or the medicines in their boxes, and your recent blood pressure readings if you have high blood pressure.

advice.title: Eating, drinking and medicines before the operation
advice.text: Follow the eating and drinking instructions you are given exactly. If there is food or liquid in your stomach during the anaesthetic, it can come up into your throat and damage your lungs. Most medicines are continued, but some must be stopped: take only the medicines you were told to take. If you feel unwell before the operation date, contact the hospital.
